formPost.title: Returning to the client
formPost.heading: Returning to the client
formPost.sub: OAuth 2.0 Form Post Response Mode — the authorization response travels in a form POST rather than in a redirect, so it never appears in a URL, in browser history or in a Referer header (RFC 9700 section 4.3).
formPost.scriptNote: The form submits itself from /oauth2/autopost.js. It is a separate resource because this service sets script-src 'none' on every response and this page relaxes it to 'self'; with scripting off the button IS the mechanism.
logout.askAppWho: The application {app} asked to sign you out of {who}. This ends your session here, and every application signed in through it is told.
logout.askApp: The application {app} asked to sign you out. This ends your session here, and every application signed in through it is told.
logout.askWho: An application asked to sign you out of {who}. This ends your session here, and every application signed in through it is told.
logout.ask: An application asked to sign you out. This ends your session here, and every application signed in through it is told.
logout.whyNoHintNoReturn: This sign-out request carried no id_token_hint, so this service cannot tell which application sent it, and it will not send you on to {uri} afterwards (RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 section 2).
logout.whyNoHint: This sign-out request carried no id_token_hint, so this service cannot tell which application sent it (RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 section 2).
logout.whyNoCookie: This sign-out request arrived without the sign-in cookie of this browser, as a form sent from another site does, so this service cannot tell which session it is for (RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 section 2).
logout.whyHintNoSid: The id_token_hint in this sign-out request carries no session identifier (sid), so this service cannot tell that it was issued to the session in this browser (RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 section 2).
logout.whyHintOtherSession: The id_token_hint in this sign-out request was issued to another session, not the one signed in to this browser (RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 section 2).
logout.whyLogoutHint: The logout_hint in this sign-out request names somebody other than the person signed in to this browser (RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 section 2).
signedOut.title: Signed out
signedOut.heading: Signed out
signedOut.ended: The session for {username} has ended, and every application signed in through it is told.
signedOut.none: There was no session to end.
signedOut.notRegistered: The post_logout_redirect_uri in this sign-out request is not one this client registered, so it was not followed. The request named {uri}; this client registered {registered} (RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 section 3).
signedOut.frontSub: OpenID Connect RP-Initiated Logout 1.0, with Front-Channel Logout 1.0
signedOut.frontEnded: The session for {username} has ended. It is the session WS-Federation and SAML 2.0 share, so those are signed out too.
signedOut.frontNone: There was no session to end. The cookie has been cleared anyway.
signedOut.returnAuto: This page returns there by itself after {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}}, once the notifications above have had time to load; the link is for a browser that does not follow a refresh.
signedOut.returnLink: A link and not a redirect: the notifications above load with this page, and a 302 would abandon them before they were sent.
logout.askWhichApp: The application {app} asked to sign you out, and this browser is signed in to {count} accounts. Which one should be signed out? Its session here ends, and every application signed in through it is told.
logout.askWhich: An application asked to sign you out, and this browser is signed in to {count} accounts. Which one should be signed out? Its session here ends, and every application signed in through it is told.
logout.whyWhich: Asked because the request did not name one of the accounts signed in to this browser (RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 section 2). The other accounts stay signed in.
authorizeError.title: This request could not be completed
authorizeError.notSent: Nothing has been sent anywhere: this request names no address this service may return you to, so the error is reported here instead (RFC 6749 section 4.1.2.1). The application that sent you here needs correcting.
authorizeError.authenticateFirst: RFC 9700 section 4.11.2: an authorization server must authenticate a person before redirecting them. Nobody is signed in on this browser, so this error is shown here rather than sent back to the application. Otherwise anybody could use this service to send a browser to an application's registered address, carrying parameters they chose, with no interaction at all.
authorizeError.continueNote: Nothing has been sent anywhere yet. Following that link delivers the error above to the application, which is what would have happened automatically if you were signed in here.
authorizeError.auto: You will be sent there automatically in {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}}.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0160: This authorization request has no redirect_uri, and one is required: without it there is nowhere to send the response.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0160-empty: This authorization request's redirect_uri is empty. A valid absolute redirect_uri is required.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0119: The redirect_uri in this request, {uri}, is not an absolute URI (RFC 9700 section 2.1).
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0120: The redirect_uri in this request, {uri}, uses the http scheme. That is allowed only for a native application returning to a loopback address (127.0.0.1, [::1] or localhost), and this is neither (RFC 9700 section 2.6).
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0121: The redirect_uri in this request, {uri}, cannot be accepted: no redirect URI is registered for this application, and RFC 9700 section 2.1 requires the redirect_uri to match a registered one exactly.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0122: The redirect_uri in this request, {uri}, is not registered for this application, and a redirect_uri must match a registered one exactly (RFC 9700 section 2.1). Registered: {registered}.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0569: The redirect_uri in this request, {uri}, is not registered for this application, and a redirect_uri must match a registered one exactly (OpenID Connect Core section 3.1.2.1). Registered: {registered}.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0273: This request has no redirect_uri, and this application has not registered exactly one that could be used in its place (OAuth 2.1 section 4.1.1).
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0274: This request has no redirect_uri, and the one this application registered cannot be used. The application's registration needs correcting.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0159: This authorization request is malformed: one of its parameters is not valid. The diagnostics below say which.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0285: This authorization request repeats a parameter, and every parameter may be sent only once.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0161: This request has no client_id. Every authorization request must name the application making it.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0162: This request names no response_type, and every authorization request must name one (RFC 6749 section 3.1.1).
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0162-unsupported: This service does not support response_type {type}.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0163: This authorization server does not offer response_type {type}.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0164: This authorization server does not offer response_mode {mode}.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0165: This authorization server does not offer code_challenge_method {method}.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0509: This request's acr_values contains a value that cannot be an acr value: a value is printable ASCII with no double quote or backslash.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0560: This request asks for an ID Token, and an OpenID Connect request must include the openid scope (OpenID Connect Core section 3.1.2.1).
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0561: This request's prompt, {prompt}, combines none with another value, which OpenID Connect Core section 3.1.2.1 forbids.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0562-implicit: This request has no nonce. Its response_type, {type}, returns an ID Token from the authorization endpoint, and for that OpenID Connect Core requires a nonce (section 3.2.2.1, the implicit flow).
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0562-hybrid: This request has no nonce. Its response_type, {type}, returns an ID Token from the authorization endpoint, and for that OpenID Connect Core requires a nonce (section 3.3.2.1, the hybrid flow).
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0563: The implicit flow may not use the http redirect_uri {uri}: only a native application returning to localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] may (OpenID Connect Core section 3.2.2.1).
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0597: Application {client} is not registered for response_type {type} (RFC 7591 section 2).
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0606: response_type none asks for no credential at all, so it cannot be combined with any other response type.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0607: response_mode query cannot carry response_type {type}: a response that returns a token or an ID Token must not be sent in the query.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0270: response_mode form_post cannot be answered at {uri}: it is a native application's private-use address, which never receives a form.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0688: This request names tenant {tenant}, which is not this authorization server's tenant. A tenant is chosen by the address the request is sent to.
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0704: The bound_key scope requires dpop_jkt on the authorization request (OpenID Connect Key Binding section 3).
refusal.STS-OAUTH-0705: The bound_key scope can be used only with response_type code (OpenID Connect Key Binding section 3).
oauthError.invalid_request: The application's request is not valid, so it could not be completed.
oauthError.unauthorized_client: This application is not allowed to make this request.
oauthError.unsupported_response_type: This service does not support the kind of response this application asked for.
oauthError.invalid_scope: The application asked for access (a scope) that this service cannot grant.
oauthError.server_error: Something went wrong on this service while it was handling the request.
oauthError.temporarily_unavailable: This service cannot handle the request right now. Try again later.
oauthError.interaction_required: You need to take part in this request, and the application asked for it to happen without showing you anything.
oauthError.login_required: You need to sign in, and the application asked not to show you a sign-in screen.
oauthError.account_selection_required: You need to choose an account, and the application asked not to show you a choice.
oauthError.consent_required: Your consent is needed, and the application asked not to show you the consent screen.
oauthError.invalid_request_uri: The request_uri in this request cannot be used.
oauthError.invalid_request_object: The request object in this request cannot be used.
oauthError.request_not_supported: This service does not accept the request parameter here.
oauthError.request_uri_not_supported: This service does not accept the request_uri parameter here.
oauthError.registration_not_supported: This service does not accept the registration parameter.
oauthError.invalid_authorization_details: The authorization details in this request cannot be accepted.
oauthError.invalid_target: The resource this request names cannot be used.
oauthError.invalid_client: The application could not be identified.
oauthError.unmet_authentication_requirem: The sign-in this application requires could not be met.
oauthError.other: The request could not be completed.
logoutRefused.unreadableTitle: This sign-out request could not be read
logoutRefused.nothingDone: Nothing has been done: you are still signed in.
logoutRefused.mayNotHaveFinished: The sign-out may not have finished. Sign out again to be sure.
logoutRefused.hintBackground: RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 section 2: when a sign-out request carries an id_token_hint, the OpenID Provider must check that it is an ID Token it issued. This one is not, so the request was refused rather than acted on.
logoutRefused.notForm: A sign-out sent with POST must be a form (application/x-www-form-urlencoded, RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 section 2). This one was {type}.
logoutRefused.malformed: This sign-out request is malformed: one of its parameters is not valid. The diagnostics below say which.
logoutRefused.failed: Something went wrong on this service while signing you out.
logoutRefused.hint.encrypted: The id_token_hint is encrypted. This service reads only the signed ID Token it issued, which is what the application should send.
logoutRefused.hint.notJwt: The id_token_hint is not a JWT, so it is not an ID Token this service issued.
logoutRefused.hint.unsigned: The id_token_hint is unsigned (alg {alg}). Every ID Token this service issues is signed, so it is not one this service issued.
logoutRefused.hint.noSecret: The id_token_hint is signed with {alg}, and application {client} has no client secret to verify it with.
logoutRefused.hint.unknownKey: The id_token_hint names key {kid} for {alg}, and this service holds no such key.
logoutRefused.hint.noKid: The id_token_hint is signed with {alg} and names no key, so this service cannot tell which of its keys to verify it with.
logoutRefused.hint.signature: The id_token_hint's signature does not verify, so it is not an ID Token this service issued.
logoutRefused.hint.issuer: The id_token_hint was issued by {iss}, and this service is {issuer}.
logoutRefused.hint.noIssuer: The id_token_hint names no issuer, and this service is {issuer}.
logoutRefused.hint.audience: The id_token_hint was issued to {aud}, not to application {client}.
